notes: No resistor: the sketch uses INPUT_PULLUP, and the image and schematic show none.

The button straddles the centre gap in columns 4 and 6. I took the pairs that are joined inside it to be the two legs in the same column. So side 1 is column 4 (1.l top, 1.r bottom) and side 2 is column 6 (2.l top, 2.r bottom). Pressing the button joins column 4 to column 6.
The blue wire goes from Leonardo pin 2 to column 6 in the top half. That is the same strip as the button's column-6 legs.
The black wire goes from the Leonardo GND pin beside 5V (GND.1) to column 4 in the bottom half. That is the same strip as the button's column-4 legs.

Row letters follow the catalogue, where the top half is rows a-e and the bottom half is f-j. The image labels its top half j-f and its bottom half e-a. I mapped the image's rows by position, so the exact row letter is approximate. The strips (column and half) are what matter, and they are right.
The Leonardo is not seated on the breadboard. It connects to the breadboard only through the two wires.
